issues.legal_issue: Evidence cannot be used to establish a materially different factual case that was not pleaded, except in the limited circumstances where the pleadings and issues substantially cover that case and the parties knowingly tried it.
material_facts: The specific-performance plaintiff pleaded that the workers’ union had refused consent to the sale because of collusion with the vendors.
The plaintiff later relied on letters said to show that the union had agreed to the sale on conditions, but the plaint was not amended to plead that alleged conditional agreement.

The letters were disputed; the person said to have supplied them was not called as a witness, and a witness’s identification of a signature did not establish the letters’ contents. The letters also contained contradictory statements.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s Division Bench was justified in refusing to consider the letters as proof of a case that had not been pleaded; the letters did not establish the alleged conditional consent.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, pleadings and issues define the case the parties must meet, and evidence cannot ordinarily establish a new case outside them. A deficiency may be overlooked only in exceptional circumstances where the pleadings and issues substantially cover the matter, the parties knew it was in issue, and they led evidence on it. The Court relied on Bachhaj Nahar v. Nilima Mandal, Bhagwati Prasad v. Chandramaul and Ram Sarup Gupta v. Bishun Narain Inter College. It also applied the principles that admitting or marking a document does not by itself prove its contents or probative value, as discussed in Shalimar Chemical Works Ltd. v. Surendra Oil and Dal Mills, H. Siddiqui v. A. Ramalingam and R.V.E. Venkatachala Gounder v. Arulmigu Viswesaraswami & V.P. Temple.

predicates.civil_specific_performance_case: A party brought a civil proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.material_factual_case_not_pleaded: A party relied on evidence to assert a material factual case different from the case set out in its pleadings.
predicates.no_amendment_to_pleadings: The party did not amend its pleadings to include that material factual case.

issues.definition: When a party in a civil specific-performance case relies on a materially different factual case that it did not plead or add by amendment, that case cannot support relief.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser cannot obtain specific performance when an agreement makes the sale conditional on the workers’ consent and the workers refuse consent; the purchaser’s unilateral waiver of that condition does not require the vendors to complete the sale.
material_facts: The agreement made the sale subject to the vendors settling with their workers and obtaining the workers’ agreement to the sale, as well as specified permissions and a change in the property’s use.
The workers’ union informed the vendors that it did not consent to the sale, and the Court did not accept the disputed letters as proof that the union had conditionally agreed.
The purchaser said he had waived the worker-consent condition, but the agreement provided that the vendors would not be bound to complete the sale if they could not obtain the workers’ agreement.
The purchaser sought specific performance, and the agreement provided for repayment of the money with interest if a required consent or permission was refused.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was contingent on the specified conditions, including worker consent. Because the workers refused consent, the agreement could not be performed and the vendors were not bound to complete the sale. The purchaser was entitled to the return of the money with the interest stipulated in the agreement, not specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the agreement according to its express conditions: the vendors were not bound to complete the sale if the workers did not agree, and failure of a required condition entitled the purchaser to the agreed repayment. The Court also considered the discretionary nature of specific performance under Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and relied on the discussion in M. Meenakshi v. Metadin Agarwal that readiness and willingness alone do not make specific performance automatic where a required sanction or condition has failed. The agreement referred to permissions under Sections 22 and 27 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, but the Court’s conclusion rested on the contractual conditions and the workers’ refusal of consent.

predicates.specific_performance_case: A party sought specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.sale_agreement_requires_worker_consent: The agreement made completion of the sale conditional on the workers agreeing to the sale.
predicates.workers_refused_consent: The workers or their representative refused to agree to the sale.

issues.definition: If a party seeks specific performance of a sale agreement that requires worker consent and the workers refuse consent, specific performance is unavailable and the agreement’s repayment consequence applies.
